# Methods

## Data provenance and curation {#sec-data}

The training corpus comprises **23,535** curated T-box riboswitch records drawn
from the T-box database (TBDB) lineage (DOI:10.1093/nar/gkaa721; accessed
2026-07-11), re-ingested through a proper-CSV parse gate that reconciles the
record count and per-record hash-identity against the upstream cleaned table
before any downstream use. Each record's taxonomy is re-placed onto a single
pinned GTDB release so that the clade boundaries used for splitting are
internally consistent. Notably, the curated corpus contains **no archaeal
records**; whether *bona fide* T-boxes exist in Archaea (and in the
under-sampled DPANN, CPR/Patescibacteria, and candidate phyla) is treated as an
open question the genome-wide scan is designed to test, not a settled negative
(PMID:36594112, DOI:10.1002/wrna.1774; PMID:31020937,
DOI:10.2174/1386207322666190425143301; accessed 2026-07-11). Dataset
construction, splits, and evaluation are reported following the DOME
recommendations for machine learning in biology (DOI:10.1093/gigascience/giae094,
PMID:39661723; accessed 2026-07-10).

## Non-circular evaluation design {#sec-eval}

Because the headline claim is a **generalization** claim — that a learned model
recovers T-boxes beyond the phylogenetic range of its training data — homology
leakage across the train/test boundary would inflate exactly the metric that is
the paper's central result. We therefore partition the corpus by a
**structure-aware, homology-clustered leave-clade-out** scheme: positives are
single-linkage clustered on consensus-column identity over per-class covariance-
model alignments (**RF00230** for class I, **TBDB001** for class II, applied
within each class and unioned), whole clusters are assigned to folds, and
clade-crossing clusters are held out, yielding a partition with maximum
held-out-to-training
consensus identity **< 0.70** (observed maximum 0.699). This design is motivated
by the documented collapse of sequence-based homology search on divergent
non-coding RNA (PMID:17151342, DOI:10.1101/gr.5890907; PMID:19861422,
DOI:10.1261/rna.1556009; accessed 2026-07-10), which is precisely the regime in
which a generalization claim must be tested. Leakage control is enforced as a
**CI-blocking test** over the real full-corpus partition on every change.

Detection is evaluated against pre-registered, blinded-frozen gates: **GATE-1**
(recall at matched precision versus a `cmsearch` baseline, with a two-part
effect-size-plus-CI-floor bar over block-resampled, macro-averaged arms),
**GATE-2** (in-distribution calibration error and a bootstrap-CI-bounded
discovery false-discovery proportion on a conservative empirical null),
**GATE-3** (a per-corpus verdict rolled up to a project-level outcome), and
**GATE-4** (per-nucleotide segmentation F1 taken as the **minimum over the three
core structural elements**, not a mean). Circularity is further controlled by a
class-II-CM-naive detector checkpoint that is never routed through the covariance
model it would otherwise memorize, and by requiring **orthogonal** (covariation,
architecture, synteny) evidence before any novel-clade discovery is confirmed.
All gate thresholds are pinned across six Architecture Decision Records
(ADR-0001…0006) and are frozen prior to unblinding.

::: {#fig-splits}
*[Figure — split-separation diagnostic. Placeholder image inserted at render
time.]*

**Figure 1. The leave-clade-out split admits no train/test homology leakage.**
All-versus-all consensus-column identity between held-out and training T-box
positives, computed over per-class covariance-model alignments (RF00230 for
class I, TBDB001 for class II). The mass of held-out
records lies below the 0.70 clustering cut (identity ≥ 0.70 links records into a
single cluster assigned wholly to one fold), so that **no** held-out record
shares ≥ 0.70 identity with any training record (observed maximum 0.699). The
tighter-cutoff sensitivity sweep is stable and conservative under tightening.
:::

## Model architecture and backbone validation {#sec-models}

Detection is two-stage. **Stage 1** scans genomic DNA with **Caduceus-PS**
(`seqlen-131k_d_model-256_n_layer-16`, 7.73 M parameters; arXiv:2403.03234,
PMID:40567809; accessed 2026-07-12), a reverse-complement-*equivariant* state-space
model, over ~1 kb windows (stride 512) — far below its 131 kb context, which is
unnecessary for ~150–350 nt loci and costly at scan throughput. A per-nucleotide
8-class segmentation head (linear, with an optional CRF transition term) emits the
element decomposition. The backbone is reverse-complement **equivariant**, not invariant:
for a hidden state $h = f(x)$ it satisfies $f(\mathrm{rc}(x)) = \mathrm{flip}(h)$ along the
sequence and channel axes, so the two strands' representations are *coupled* rather than
identical. A strand-agnostic scalar therefore cannot by itself orient a locus, but the
directional information survives, and the reverse-complement channels are combined by
concatenation — deliberately not by an order-destroying average, which would collapse the
element order — so that strand is resolved downstream from the *predicted element order*.
**Stage 2** re-ranks candidates
with **RiNALMo-giga** (650 M parameters; 33 layers, hidden 1280; pretrained on ~36 M
non-coding RNAs and reported to generalise to unseen RNA families for secondary
structure; PMID:40593636, DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-60872-5; accessed 2026-07-13),
accessed through the transformers-native `multimolecule/rinalmo-giga` mirror at a pinned
revision.

Three Stage-1 architecture choices — reverse-complement combination, segmentation head, and
backbone size/effective context — were fixed by a pre-registered ablation rather than by
default. Each leg reused the promoted training protocol unchanged (`inner_train`,
positives-only, seed 42, the 1024/512 geometry) and was scored on a disjoint 830-record,
469-homology-cluster selection fold with cluster-blocked bootstrap intervals; the promoted
configuration supplies the baseline row. Ranked on the conservative lower interval bound, a
arms were **replicated**, and separation is judged only against replicate-widened intervals.
Independent re-runs reproduce closely — spread 0.0001 across three replicates of the smallest
backbone, 0.0000 across two of the 1.93 M backbone, and 0.0006 across two of the baseline —
so the intervals below are not single-run artefacts. The baseline (0.9393/0.9386, widened
interval [0.9125, 0.9576]) and the 1.93 M-parameter backbone (0.9191, [0.8920, 0.9412]) are
**not distinguishable**, which is a statement about resolution rather than equivalence.
Exactly one arm separates, and it separates downward: the 471 k-parameter checkpoint reaches
0.8890 with a replicate-widened interval [0.8581, 0.9047] lying entirely below the baseline's
lower bound, locating the floor of the downward search. Because the size search is
throughput-driven — a validation column alone cannot deliver it — forward-only scan rate was
measured for each checkpoint at the same window geometry on one GPU: 69.5, 268.4 and
423.5 windows/s (1.0×, 3.86×, 6.10×). The 1.93 M checkpoint therefore buys 3.86× scan
throughput at no *resolvable* accuracy cost, while the 471 k checkpoint's 6.10× is bought at
a measurable one. Two arms are reported without a separation verdict because they were not
replicated: the CRF head (0.9416, [0.9196, 0.9571]) and the gated reverse-complement
combination. The latter is withheld for cause — its two runs disagreed (0.9242 vs 0.7568),
with the whole difference in one element whose ranking quality was unchanged (antiterminator
AUPRC 0.9843 → 0.9705) but whose boundary agreement collapsed (IoU 0.8590 → 0.6087), i.e. a
decision-threshold shift under uncalibrated outputs; since the two runs were at different
commits and no two exist at one commit, we do not attribute it and do not report the arm.
Both smaller checkpoints are pretrained at 1 kb against production's 131 kb,
so this is a joint size × pretraining-context arm and no difference may be attributed to
parameter count alone; the CRF arm is graded under the frozen reconcile→argmax operator, so
Viterbi decoding is not exercised and the arm measures the CRF as a training signal only. The
order-destroying averaged RC combination is not an arm of this ablation: it is excluded by
design, because the strand resolver derives orientation from predicted element order. These
are selection-fold measurements used to fix architecture, not generalization results.

Because the central claim of this work is a **generalization** claim, neither backbone is
assumed to transfer: each was gated before use. Caduceus-PS transfer was tested in two
parts — a non-binding frozen-embedding linear-separability pre-filter (AUROC 0.992 on
held-out bacterial T-box windows vs GC-matched prokaryotic background) and a **binding**
per-nucleotide segmentation probe on a leave-clade-out held-out smoke set, which reached
a minimum per-nucleotide F1 over the three core elements (Stem I, Specifier,
Antiterminator) of **0.9999** against a background-only baseline of 0.0, and reproduced
on a seeded re-run within a tolerance pinned *a priori*. Neither probe is the paper's
generalization result, and they are limited in different ways: the pre-filter scores a
**cluster-grouped, homology-safe** probe split (grouped by homology cluster, so no cluster
spans its train/test boundary) and therefore measures **cluster-level separability of
frozen features**, while the binding segmentation probe fine-tunes and grades on the *same*
held-out loci and is therefore a measurement of **learnability/expressivity only**.
Generalization is graded at GATE-4 on the full leave-clade-out partition (@sec-eval) —
a strictly harder split, since taxonomic order still spans the pre-filter's probe boundary
— and all of these loci are held out from the training corpus, so the go/no-go cannot
contaminate it. Adopting the RiNALMo mirror was
gated on reproducing the published ArchiveII nine-family leave-one-family-out
secondary-structure generalization. That refit-based criterion **failed** by 2.3 pp
(nine-family mean 0.696 vs 0.719 published) and is reported as failed; the mirror was
nonetheless adopted on stronger direct evidence — its encoder is **bit-identical** to the
official release (497/497 tensors, max |Δ| 0.0), and RiNALMo's own released fine-tuned
weights reproduce the published figures to ~0.1 pp through this pipeline — locating the
gap in fresh-head refit variance rather than in the backbone. Stage-2 fine-tuning uses
LoRA (`r=16, α=32, dropout=0.05, target_modules="all-linear"`; bf16 + gradient
checkpointing; 12,840,432 of 662,079,483 parameters trainable, 1.94%), which a measured
smoke confirms fits a single 16 GB RTX A4000 at **1.484 GiB peak**, with
FlashAttention-2 verified by forward on `sm_86`. Two contingencies are implemented and
neither is triggered, for distinct reasons: a DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 / FSDP `FULL_SHARD`
full-fine-tune path, which the LoRA memory measurement above makes unnecessary; and a
Stage-1 backbone-fallback ladder (frozen-embedding probe, GTDB continued-pretraining,
Nucleotide-Transformer-multispecies), which the transfer go/no-go having passed leaves
unused.

# Results

## Stage-1 segments T-box elements accurately in distribution, and substantially less so across held-out taxonomic orders {#sec-gate4}

**GATE-4 passes.** The minimum per-nucleotide class F1 over the three core
structural elements — the gated statistic, deliberately a minimum rather than a
mean, so a strong element cannot mask a weak one — is **0.952** against a
pre-registered floor of 0.80, with a homology-cluster-blocked bootstrap 95%
interval of **[0.943, 0.960]** (1,029 clusters, 2,000 resamples) that clears the
floor by its lower bound. Per element: Stem I 0.975, Antiterminator 0.970, and
Specifier 0.952, the minimum and therefore the statistic. Element extents are
recovered, not merely nucleotides labelled: boundary IoU is 0.951 (Stem I), 0.941
(Antiterminator) and 0.908 (Specifier), computed through the overlapping-window
log-mean-exp reconciliation operator the scanner itself deploys, so these are not
artefacts of the 512-nt tiling grid. Non-core classes are reported but not gated;
Stem III is weakest (F1 0.880, IoU 0.786). Specifier codon localisation is exact
to all three nucleotides in 89.8% of scorable loci and overlaps truth in 98.7%.

Two properties of this measurement constrain how it should be read. First, the
graded artefact is an **evaluation twin**, not the shipped detector: the shipped
checkpoint trained on the entire in-distribution fold, leaving no held-out
population, so a second checkpoint was trained with the graded clusters withheld
(8,303 → 7,099 records; 1,204 records in 1,031 clusters removed) and graded in its
place. The twin saw strictly less data, so 0.952 is a **conservative proxy** for
the shipped model rather than a measurement of it, and the graded population shares
zero clusters and zero records with the twin's training fold. Second, the graded
population is 98.7% Firmicutes (1,185/1,201 records) — the corpus composition that
remains once the leave-one-order-out holdout is removed, not a sampling decision.

**The same checkpoint generalises far less well across taxonomic orders.** On the
leave-one-order-out holdout (21.0 M positions, macro-averaged across 30 held-out
orders), per-element F1 falls to 0.765 (Antiterminator), 0.721 (Stem I) and 0.715
(Specifier), with per-order minima approaching zero. This read is reported and
explicitly **not** gated here: GATE-4 grades in-distribution segmentation quality,
whereas the generalization claim this work makes is graded at GATE-1 (@sec-eval)
on precisely this axis. The gap between 0.95 in distribution and ~0.72 across
orders is the quantity that matters for novel-clade discovery, and it is reported
alongside the passing gate rather than after it (@fig-gate4).

::: {#fig-gate4}
*[Figure — Stage-1 segmentation quality. Placeholder image inserted at render
time.]*

**Figure 2. Stage-1 segmentation is accurate in distribution and degrades
sharply across held-out taxonomic orders.** Per-nucleotide class F1 for each of
the eight segmentation classes, measured on the GATE-4 evaluation twin through
the overlapping-window log-mean-exp reconciliation operator the scanner deploys.
*Left*, the in-distribution homology-clustered reference population (1,201
records, 1,029 clusters, 2.98 M nucleotides): the three core elements that
constitute the gate — Stem I 0.975, Antiterminator 0.970, Specifier 0.952 — are
marked, with the gated statistic (their **minimum**, 0.952) and its
cluster-blocked bootstrap 95% interval [0.943, 0.960] shown against the
pre-registered 0.80 floor; non-core classes are plotted but excluded from the
gate, Stem III being the weakest at 0.880. *Right*, the same checkpoint on the
leave-one-order-out holdout (21.0 M nucleotides), macro-averaged over 30 held-out
orders, where the core elements fall to 0.765 / 0.721 / 0.715 and per-order
minima approach zero; whiskers span the per-order range. The two panels share an
axis deliberately: the vertical distance between them, not the height of the left
panel, is what bears on discovery in unrepresented lineages. The gate is graded
on the left panel only, and on the twin rather than the shipped checkpoint, so
the left-hand values are a conservative proxy for the deployed model.
:::

The cross-source label-noise ceiling that would license recalibrating the 0.80
floor is **not estimable** from the available crystal structures: Antiterminator
and Specifier are resolved to a residue extent in 0 of the 9 depositions (Stem I in
5, Stem II in 1), so no cross-source agreement over the gated elements can be
computed. The recalibration path is therefore closed and the floor stands as
pre-registered — a ceiling estimated from N ≤ 9 must not be allowed to lower the
bar in one direction only. All figures above are computed on the uncalibrated
posterior.
